explanation: Subtract each visited value from the target. Only a leaf with zero remaining weight completes a root-to-leaf path. A long remainder prevents intermediate sums from overflowing 32 bits.
timeComplexity: O(n) in the worst case. Each node is explored at most once; early success can shorten the search, and recursion retains at most h frames.
spaceComplexity: O(h) recursion stack for tree height h. Each active frame holds a node and residual target; no complete path list is kept.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: At each node, the remainder equals the target minus all values on the path through that node. A root-to-leaf path therefore has the target sum exactly when a leaf has remainder zero. Recursing into both children explores every possible root-to-leaf path; using long avoids false matches from 32-bit wraparound.
walkthrough: Use tree [7,4,3,null,2,5] and target 13. Visiting 7 leaves remainder 6; its left child 4 leaves 2; that node’s right leaf 2 leaves 0. The path 7→4→2 therefore proves the result true. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: An empty tree has no root-to-leaf path and returns false.
A nonleaf with remainder zero is not sufficient.
Negative values are handled by subtraction without pruning.
Intermediate sums may exceed int range even when the target fits.
